messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: latency.p95 for /v1/generate crossed threshold (3.2s) in prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-15T16:05:01Z. Page: Sam (oncall). Detect window: 5m. Autotriage: elevated queue-wait + kernel sched stall signals. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/2765432101
Sam (oncall): Got it — investigating. Initial impact: p50 from 120ms -> 180ms, p95 from 1.2s -> 3.6s. Customers seeing increased tail latency. Triage: are there recent deploys? :eyes:
Maria - SRE: Confirming spike across multiple dedicated pools in us-west-2. Noted a coincident kernel rollout 35m ago to instance image v2026-03-15-k2 on node-pools gpux-*-usw2. Pulling node upgrade history now.
Devon - Kernel: I can check kernel changelogs. We bumped preempt config and sched patches — there was a backported runqueue/sched patch that can affect CFS latency.
Jamal - ML Infra: ML-serving traces show increased tail from model runtime step AND queuing in the runtime. Trace span breakdown: queue_wait (avg 25ms -> 480ms), model_infer (avg stable), first_token_delay increased. See span view: https://traces.internal/trace/2765432101
Sam (oncall): Can someone share perf counters / pmu snapshots from affected hosts? We need to see runqueue length, CPU steal, context-switch rates.
Maria - SRE: Uploading sample logs + perf output to blobstore: gs://redwood-debug/2765432101/perf-samples.tar.gz
Maria - SRE: Quick logs (node=node-usa-gpux-11):
```
Mar 15 15:40:12 node kernel: sched: runqueue length 48  p90
Mar 15 15:40:12 node kernel: rcu_preempt detected stall on CPU 3
Mar 15 15:40:13 node dockerd: container runtime blocked for 600ms
```
Devon - Kernel: rcu_preempt stalls + runqueue spikes line up with kernel change. Hypothesis A: scheduler patch interacted poorly with our workload bursts -> runqueue grow and long latency. Hypothesis B: unrelated noisy neighbor (I/O) causing CPU steal.
Jamal - ML Infra: Perf top from one host shows syscalls rose ~3x and softirq time increased. `perf record` attached in tar. Model-level throughput stable, but queuing backlog due to slower scheduling.
Sam (oncall): Mitigation options: 1) Roll back kernel change on a subset (canary) 2) Evacuate pods off newest nodes to older image 3) Add temporary autoscale/burst capacity in another region 4) Throttle batching (reduce batch size) to reduce runqueue pressure. Thoughts?
Devon - Kernel: Easiest fast mitigation is to cordon + drain a few nodes of v2026-03-15-k2 and schedule onto v2026-03-10-k1 images. I'll prepare the node list.
Maria - SRE: I'm starting controlled drain of three affected nodes (gpux-11/12/13). Will shift traffic; doing one-at-a-time. Tracking impacts in the dashboard.
Claire - Support: Heads up, two customers (acct-431, acct-882) opened support tickets reporting timeouts. Adding them to status page note.
Sam (oncall): Doing quick change: reduced default batch size from 8 -> 4 in routing policy for us-west-2 (hot path) as temporary throttle. Pushing config now: `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/route/scale -d '{"region":"us-west-2","batch_max":4}'`
Sam (oncall): Batch throttle deployed. Observed p95 drop from 3.6s -> 2.1s in 2min. Still above baseline but improving.
Maria - SRE: Drain completed for gpux-11. Monitoring. p95 trending down to 1.4s.
Devon - Kernel: I'll assemble exact set of kernel commits. Preliminary blame: commit 0x9f3b7c touched `sched/core.c` throttling logic. Reverting that at host-image level requires new image build — longer path. For faster rollback, we can move workloads to older image as Maria is doing.
Jamal - ML Infra: Captured perf counters across drained nodes vs old nodes: runqueue avg 3 -> 0.6, ctxt_switches 1800/s -> 220/s. That maps to improved latencies. Attaching sample numbers in thread.
Sam (oncall): Good mitigation path. Next: customer communications and handoff. I'm escalating to oncall rotation lead — Anita will take over in 30m. Anita, TL;DR: kernel rollout correlated with p95 spike; we drained affected nodes and throttled batching; p95 improved from 3.6s -> 1.2s.
Anita (next-oncall): On it. I'll continue monitoring for 2 hours, verify no regressions in other regions, and coordinate with Kernel/Infra for RCA doc.
Devon - Kernel: Action items for RCA: collect `git bisect` range, perf captures, full ftrace on repro node, boot logs, and exact list of node images rolled. I'll work with infra to root cause commit-level.
Maria - SRE: Timeline summary (for RCA):
- 15:30 UTC: batch kernel image rollout started (v2026-03-15-k2)
- 15:40 UTC: IncidentBot alert for latency.p95 > 3s (root message ts 2765432101)
- 15:42 UTC: Sam throttled batch size to 4 (temporary config)
- 15:45 UTC: Started cordon/drain gpux-11 (first node)
- 15:50 UTC: p95 trending down to ~1.4s
- 16:05 UTC: All three nodes drained, traffic on older images
- 16:15 UTC: p95 back to baseline ~1.1s
Hypotheses: scheduler patch regression vs noisy neighbor; current evidence leans scheduler regression.
Sam (oncall): Owners: RCA lead: Devon (kernel), Data collection: Jamal and Maria, Customer comms: Claire, Postmortem writeup: Anita.
Devon - Kernel: I'll open the RFC/gerrit and link to this thread. Expect initial RCA draft within 24h.
Anita (next-oncall): I'll update the status page and follow up on support tickets. Leaving a 30m overlap. Sam handing off now. :white_check_mark:
Sam (oncall): Handing off to Anita. Leaving logs and notes. If anything spikes, poke me.
IncidentBot: Incident status changed to mitigated by user action at 2765433600. Followup: create postmortem within 72h and tag `incidents/latency-regression`.
Anita (next-oncall): Noted — creating postmortem doc: https://docs.internal/postmortems/2765432101-latency-kernel-rollback . Will include perf samples and timeline.
Claire - Support: Adding impacted customers to PM followup, drafting proactive outreach.
Sam (oncall): Thanks team. Good mitigation. We'll reconvene async for RCA.
